title: CARE: Context-Aware Ranking Evolution with Executable Scoring Programs for Budgeted Reaction Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2606.14581v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: High-throughput experimentation can evaluate many reaction conditions, yet combinatorial condition spaces still exceed the available experiment budget. This makes experiment selection a sequential decision problem: each new condition must be chosen from limited observations before its outcome is known. LLMs can express task-specific selection logic. A direct recommendation, however, is neither a persistent executable object that can be validated and revised nor an independently auditable decision rule. We introduce CARE, a reference-conditioned controller that separates program synthesis from experiment selection. An LLM writes an executable scoring program that ranks the remaining conditions, while a non-LLM reference policy supplies a numerical candidate and support summary. translated_title: CARE：面向预算受限反应优化的上下文感知排序演化与可执行评分程序
translated_abstract: 高通量实验可以评估许多反应条件，然而组合式的条件空间仍然超出了可用的实验预算。这使得实验选择成为一个序贯决策问题：每个新条件必须在结果已知之前从有限的观测中选出。大语言模型可以表达任务特定的选择逻辑，然而直接推荐既不是可验证和修订的持久可执行对象，也不是可独立审计的决策规则。我们提出了CARE，一个将程序合成与实验选择分离的参考条件控制器。大语言模型编写一个可执行的评分程序来对剩余条件进行排序，同时一个非LLM的参考策略提供数值候选和支持摘要。CARE从程序中形成一个可选的替代方案，应用参考条件干预门将其与参考进行比较，并记录……（原文摘要在此截断）
tldr: CARE通过让大语言模型编写可执行、可审计的评分程序来对反应条件排序，并借助参考条件干预门与非LLM参考策略进行对比控制，从而解决预算受限反应优化中的序贯实验选择问题。
en_tdlr: CARE tackles sequential experiment selection in budgeted reaction optimization by having LLMs write executable, auditable scoring programs to rank conditions, with a reference-conditioned intervention gate comparing them against a non-LLM reference policy.
